prompt.es: Explica una costumbre de tu familia a un visitante con matices y una comparación.

answer.text: In my family, Sunday lunch is a custom that we have had for many years. By and large, relatives tend to arrive around noon, and a visitor is always welcome to join us. For example, last week my cousin brought a friend from Japan, and we simply added one more chair. We usually share one big dish from the centre of the table. In some countries people eat from separate plates, whereas in mine we like to pass the food around. Neither way is better; each tradition makes sense at home. It may seem unusual at first, but visitors quickly feel at home because everybody talks, laughs and asks questions. I hope you will join us one Sunday, and I promise to explain every custom with a smile.
accepted: In my family, Sunday lunch is a custom that we have had for many years. By and large, relatives tend to arrive around noon, and a visitor is always welcome to join us. For example, last week my cousin brought a friend from Japan, and we simply added one more chair. We usually share one big dish from the centre of the table. In some countries people eat from separate plates, whereas in mine we like to pass the food around. Neither way is better; each tradition makes sense at home. It may seem unusual at first, but visitors quickly feel at home because everybody talks, laughs and asks questions. I hope you will join us one Sunday, and I promise to explain every custom with a smile.

Every Friday my family has pizza night, a tradition we started when I was a child. As a rule, everybody is home by seven, and the children tend to choose what we eat. For instance, my little brother always asks for cheese and tomato, and we all laugh. Visitors are welcome too, and they usually bring a dessert. In other countries families often eat at the table, whereas in mine we sit on the sofa and watch a film. Neither way is wrong; it is simply a different habit. At first it may feel a bit strange, but guests normally relax after the first bite. I would love to have you with us one Friday, and I promise to share the best part.

feedback.es: El texto presenta la costumbre, matiza dos generalizaciones, da un ejemplo concreto y compara con respeto.

title.en: Host a guest, avoid the clash

prompt.es: Explica dos costumbres, aclara un malentendido y responde con tacto a tu invitado.

answer.text: Welcome, Carlos, and please feel at home! In my family we tend to eat dinner at six, and by and large everybody helps to set the table. Let me clarify something about last night: we did not mean to be rude when we started eating without you. I apologise, because I should have explained that we usually do not wait after seven. You asked a good question: why do we not talk more at dinner? Some families tend to be quieter, and ours likes to enjoy the food first. It is only a habit, and nobody is upset. Tomorrow we will talk as much as you like, and I will show you the city.
accepted: Welcome, Carlos, and please feel at home! In my family we tend to eat dinner at six, and by and large everybody helps to set the table. Let me clarify something about last night: we did not mean to be rude when we started eating without you. I apologise, because I should have explained that we usually do not wait after seven. You asked a good question: why do we not talk more at dinner? Some families tend to be quieter, and ours likes to enjoy the food first. It is only a habit, and nobody is upset. Tomorrow we will talk as much as you like, and I will show you the city.

Hello, Carlos, make yourself at home! As a rule, my family has breakfast together at eight, and we tend to be quiet because we are still sleepy. Let me explain something about this morning: we did not mean to ignore you. I am sorry, because I should have told you about our custom. That is a fair question: why is nobody talking? In some houses people talk a lot at breakfast, whereas in ours we like silence and coffee. It is only a habit, and nobody is angry. At lunch we will talk as much as you like, and I promise to ask you about your country.

feedback.es: El texto da la bienvenida, explica costumbres con matices, aclara el malentendido sin culpar y responde con tacto.
